quizzes.title: Artemis Accords: Practice Quiz (MCQ)
quizzes.passage: NASA's Artemis Programme is named after the Moon Goddess of Greek mythology. Its stated objective is to land humans on the Moon, including the first woman and the first person of colour to stand on the lunar surface. The programme is being carried out in stages. Artemis I was an unmanned mission that began with the launch of a spacecraft named Orion on the Space Launch System. Orion has a crew module and a service module. Artemis II is a crewed mission in which astronauts will travel around the Moon and return to Earth without landing on it. Its crew of four includes the first Canadian and the first non-American to fly on a lunar mission. The mission is expected to last about ten days, following a free-return trajectory before the spacecraft splashes down in the Pacific Ocean. It will lift off from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida, USA. The programme depends on partnerships. The European Space Agency and the Canadian Space Agency are named as its international collaborators. The planned Lunar Gateway Station is meant to serve as a docking point for astronauts and to facilitate scientific research. Artemis III is the stage meant to return humans to the Moon. The Artemis Accords form part of the same international picture.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT among the founding members of the Artemis Accords?
questions.explanation: India joined the Accords in 2023 as its 27th member, so it was not one of the founding members.

questions.q: Besides the Moon, which bodies do the common principles of the Artemis Accords cover?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Accords cover the Moon, Mars, comets and asteroids for peaceful purposes.

questions.q: Along with NASA, which body established the Artemis Accords?
questions.explanation: The Accords were established by the US State Department and NASA together.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Artemis Accords build upon the Outer Space Treaty of 1967.
Reason (R): The Artemis Accords are not legally binding.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the non-binding nature of the Accords does not explain why they build on the 1967 treaty.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Announcement of the Artemis Accords by NASA   ->   A. 2020
II. Founding members other than the US State Department and NASA   ->   B. Seven
III. India's entry into the Accords   ->   C. As the 27th member
IV. Russia and China   ->   D. Not part of the Accords
questions.explanation: NASA announced the Accords in 2020, seven other founding members joined, India was the 27th member, and Russia and China are not part of the Accords.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Artemis Accords:
I. The United Arab Emirates is one of the founding members of the Artemis Accords.
II. Russia is one of the founding members of the Artemis Accords.
III. Luxembourg is one of the founding members of the Artemis Accords.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The UAE and Luxembourg are founding members, while Russia is not part of the Accords.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Artemis Accords:
I. The Artemis Accords set out a set of principles and guidelines for international cooperation in space exploration.
II. The Artemis Accords are legally binding on their members.
III. The Indian Space Research Organisation is one of the founding members of the Artemis Accords.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only the statement on principles and guidelines is correct, because the Accords are not legally binding and ISRO is not a founding member.

quizzes.title: Chandrayaan Missions: Practice Quiz (MCQ)
quizzes.passage: India's lunar exploration missions are known as the Chandrayaan series. Chandrayaan-1 was India's first lunar mission, and it mapped the surface of the Moon in unprecedented detail. Chandrayaan-4 is India's fourth mission to the Moon, and it follows the earlier missions in the series. Its planned work includes two launches, the development and realisation of its spacecraft, and external Deep Space Network support. Instruments from NASA and the European Space Agency will also be mounted on a rover of Chandrayaan-5, which is planned as a further lunar exploration mission. The Soviet Union was the first nation to land on the Moon, and the United States followed with the Apollo mission, which took place in 1969 and carried astronauts to the lunar surface. Neil Armstrong became the first person to step onto the Moon, and he was joined by Edwin 'Buzz' Aldrin. The United States is also the only country to have landed humans on the Moon. China's Chang'e mission also landed on the Moon. Odysseus was a lander developed in the United States that achieved the first soft lunar landing by a private company. It was the second private attempt to land on the Moon, after the failure of the Peregrine lander.

questions.q: Which country landed on the Moon with the SLIM mission in 2024?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Japan became the fifth nation to land on the Moon with SLIM in 2024.

questions.q: In which year was Chandrayaan-2 launched?
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-2 was launched in 2019 and carried an orbiter, the Vikram lander and the Pragyan rover.

questions.q: Which agency is responsible for the lunar rover of Chandrayaan-5?
questions.explanation: The booklet says JAXA is responsible for the lunar rover while ISRO handles the lander.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Chandrayaan-3 was a second attempt after Chandrayaan-2.
Reason (R): Chandrayaan-2 carried an orbiter, the Vikram lander and the Pragyan rover.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the components of Chandrayaan-2 do not explain why Chandrayaan-3 was a second attempt.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Chandrayaan-1   ->   A. Water ice found in polar craters
II. Chandrayaan-3   ->   B. Landing point Shiv Shakti
III. Chandrayaan-4   ->   C. Bringing rock samples back to Earth
IV. Chandrayaan-5   ->   D. Joint initiative of ISRO and JAXA
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-1 found water ice, Chandrayaan-3 landed at Shiv Shakti, Chandrayaan-4 aims to bring rock samples back and Chandrayaan-5 is an ISRO-JAXA initiative.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chandrayaan missions:
I. Chandrayaan-4 is slated for launch in 2028.
II. Chandrayaan-2 was launched in 2023.
III. Chandrayaan-3 used the GSLV Mk III launch vehicle.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-4 is slated for 2028 and Chandrayaan-3 used GSLV Mk III, while Chandrayaan-2 was launched in 2019.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chandrayaan missions:
I. Chandrayaan-4 includes special tests for design validation.
II. Chandrayaan-3 was India's first lunar mission.
III. The Chandrayaan-5 mission is led by NASA.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only the statement on design validation is correct, since Chandrayaan-1 was India's first lunar mission and Chandrayaan-5 is an ISRO-JAXA initiative.

questions.q: In which year did the Soviet Union's Luna 9 make the first lunar landing? (year)
questions.explanation: The Soviet Union's Luna 9 landed on the Moon in 1966.

questions.q: In which year did China's Chang'e mission land on the Moon? (year)
questions.explanation: China's Chang'e mission landed on the Moon in 2013.

questions.q: Which company developed the Odysseus lander? (company name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Odysseus was developed by Intuitive Machines (USA).

questions.q: Which launch vehicle was used for the Odysseus lander? (name)
questions.explanation: The Odysseus lander was launched on a Falcon 9.

questions.q: Which launch vehicle is listed for the two launches of the Chandrayaan-4 mission? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The Chandrayaan-4 mission includes two launches of the Launch Vehicle Mark-3 (LVM-3).
